scope.chapter: Normal Modal Logic — Syntax and Semantics

findings.finding: The counterexample calls M-prime a model while displaying its three components with set braces, unlike the ordered triple in the frozen relational-model definition and in the same section's earlier model examples.
findings.controlling_evidence: The semantic clauses use the first component as worlds, the second as accessibility, and the third as valuation; their roles require an ordered triple.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use the existing model-triple macro at this one occurrence, disclose the repair adjacent to it, and leave the English source frozen.

findings.finding: The counterexample gives V-prime(p) only, whereas the model definition requires a valuation for every propositional variable.
findings.controlling_evidence: The two counterexample formulas use p alone. Setting the truth set of every other variable q to the empty set makes V-prime total without affecting either truth value.
findings.required_translation_handling: Specify V-prime(q)=empty for all other variables and disclose that completion adjacent to the model description.
